summary.course: The patient, a structural engineer, presented to the Emergency Department following a fall from a ladder at a construction site, resulting in a deformed right wrist. Radiographs confirmed a complex distal radius fracture. He underwent successful ORIF with a volar locking plate under general anesthesia. Intraoperative nerve stimulation was used to ensure median nerve integrity. Post-operatively, pain was managed with scheduled analgesics and a volar splint. Edema was addressed with elevation and cryotherapy. He progressed well through physiotherapy, demonstrating adequate finger ROM and grip strength by discharge day. He is neurologically intact in the right hand. Patient is cleared for light sedentary work but must avoid heavy lifting or manual vibration tools for 12 weeks.

summary.course: The patient, a property manager, presented to the ER with sudden onset periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Imaging confirmed acute appendicitis. She underwent a successful laparoscopic appendectomy on the day of admission. Postoperatively, she experienced a mild ileus, managed with IV fluids and gradual mobilization. Bowel function returned on hospital day 2. Electrolytes remained stable, and she was transitioned to oral fluids and a soft diet. At discharge, she was pain-controlled on oral analgesics, tolerating a regular diet, and afebrile.

summary.course: The patient, a warehouse supervisor, presented to the trauma bay following a fall from a loading dock platform. Initial imaging confirmed a displaced fracture of the left distal radius. He underwent successful closed reduction and percutaneous pinning under local anesthesia and conscious sedation. Intraoperative fluoroscopy confirmed stable anatomical alignment. Postoperatively, pain was managed with scheduled NSAIDs and breakthrough oxycodone. He demonstrated excellent neurovascular status in the left hand throughout his stay. He was able to perform basic activities of daily living with his right hand and was cleared for discharge with strict weight-bearing restrictions on the left extremity. Blood pressure remained stable on his current antihypertensive regimen.
